title: My Mom Said My Games Were Waking Up Our Whole House #shorts

cast.boy: a stick-figure boy with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, short spiky black hair and a red hoodie
cast.mom: a stick-figure mother with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, long curly red hair in a ponytail and a purple sweater

lines.text: Mom said my video games kept waking our whole house, so what really woke us?
lines.label: hook
lines.headline: what really woke us
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, long curly red hair in a ponytail and purple sweater, standing in a dark upstairs hallway at night, hands on hips, frowning, pointing at exactly one closed bedroom door, moonlight from a window

lines.text: At three every morning, a tiny beep went off, exactly like my game's low-health warning.
lines.label: the beep
lines.headline: beep at three
lines.image: close-up of {boy}, the only person in the picture, short spiky black hair and red hoodie, sitting up in bed in a dark bedroom at night, eyes wide, both hands over his ears, faint curved sound lines in the air

lines.text: Mom, wearing two sweaters to save on heating, said only gamers are awake at three.
lines.label: the plant
lines.headline: two sweaters
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, long curly red hair in a ponytail and purple sweater, wearing a second thick gray sweater over her purple sweater, arms crossed, shivering, stern face, in a chilly dim living room at night

lines.text: She locked my console in her bedroom closet, yet that night the beep came anyway.
lines.label: console gone
lines.headline: console locked away
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, long curly red hair in a ponytail and purple sweater, standing at an open bedroom closet at night holding exactly one small flat black game console box with a plus-shaped d-pad printed on its side in both hands, the only console in the picture, frowning, no TV, no screen and no monitor anywhere in the picture

lines.text: She said I'd hidden another handheld, took away my phone, and searched my entire bedroom.
lines.label: phone gone
lines.headline: room searched
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, long curly red hair in a ponytail and purple sweater, kneeling to look under a bed in a messy kid's bedroom, shining exactly one flashlight, holding exactly one smartphone in her other hand, the only phone in the picture, suspicious face

lines.text: I cried into my pillow that night, punished for a beep I never even made.
lines.label: alone
lines.headline: crying alone
lines.image: close-up of {boy}, the only person in the picture, short spiky black hair and red hoodie, lying in bed hugging a pillow, a single tear running down his cheek, dark bedroom

lines.text: Smoke alarms beep when batteries die, so next afternoon I tested every one; all worked.
lines.label: red herring
lines.headline: every alarm passed
lines.image: {boy} is the only person in the picture, short spiky black hair and red hoodie, standing on a small step stool in a sunny hallway, pressing the button on exactly one round white smoke alarm on the ceiling, the only smoke alarm in the picture, plain with no words or numbers, relieved face

lines.text: At three I crept down the hall, tracking the beep like enemy footsteps in games.
lines.label: gamer ear
lines.headline: tracking the beep
lines.image: {boy} is the only person in the picture, short spiky black hair and red hoodie, tiptoeing down a dark hallway at night, crouched low like a sneaking game hero, one hand cupped behind his ear, focused face, moonlight

lines.text: It led me directly to the hallway smoke alarm, the very one that passed.
lines.label: the twist
lines.headline: the alarm that passed
lines.image: close-up of {boy}, the only person in the picture, short spiky black hair and red hoodie, in a dark hallway looking straight up, mouth open in surprise, at exactly one round white smoke alarm on the ceiling with one tiny red light glowing, the only smoke alarm in the picture, plain with no words or numbers

lines.text: Weak alarm batteries lose power in the cold, so they chirp at night, then recover.
lines.label: real reason
lines.headline: cold weak battery
lines.image: close-up of {boy}, the only person in the picture, short spiky black hair and red hoodie, in a chilly dark hallway holding up exactly one small rectangular battery with frost on its edges, the only battery in the picture, plain with no words or numbers, shivering, knowing face

lines.text: Mom turned the heating way down every night, so our house was coldest around three.
lines.label: Mom's heat
lines.headline: heat turned down
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, long curly red hair in a ponytail and purple sweater, turning exactly one plain round wall thermostat dial with no words or numbers, the only thermostat in the picture, at night in cold blue light, her breath showing as a small puff

lines.text: New battery, no beeping, console back, but Mom swears it sounded exactly like my game.
lines.label: the ending
lines.headline: console back, Mom swears
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, long curly red hair in a ponytail and purple sweater, in a warm sunny morning living room, holding out exactly one small flat black game console box with a plus-shaped d-pad printed on its side in both hands, handing it toward the viewer, the only console in the picture, one eyebrow raised, unconvinced grumpy face, no TV, no screen and no monitor anywhere in the picture
